samples.question: The image shows one square panel enclosed by a thick border and ruled into an 11 by 11 grid of square cells. Exactly one of the four border corners is drawn as a filled thickened block; that is the marked corner, and the cell of the grid touching it is the marked corner cell. A few cells carry a filled round dot. Now build a new 11 by 11 pattern on the same grid with this rule: ink a cell of the new pattern when the rectangular block of cells that runs from the marked corner cell to that cell, taking every row between their two rows and every column between their two columns and including both, contains an odd number of dots; leave that cell blank when the block contains an even number of dots. Apply the rule to all 121 cells, keeping the panel in the orientation shown. The inked cells of the new pattern form a shape that most closely matches one of these five symbols: arch (a bridge: two upright legs joined by a bar along the bottom, open at the top), bars (two separate horizontal bars, one near the top and one near the bottom), ring (a hollow rectangular frame, filled on all four sides), tee (a horizontal bar along the top with a vertical stem hanging from its middle), zed (two offset blocks forming a Z-like step, the upper block shifted to the left and the lower block shifted to the right). Which symbol is it? Answer with one word.
